newsitem.title: USA: CME expels trader for S&P 500 dealings.
newsitem.headline: CME expels trader for S&P 500 dealings.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said it had expelled a trader for major offenses involving a trade in its S&P 500 futures contract and suspended another trader for five days for minor offenses.
The exchange said it permanently barred Jay Feld from its membership and from access to the trading floor effective December 23.

The exchange said its Floor Practice Committee, Finance Division, found that Feld had deliberately failed to submit a trading card containing a losing trade in S&P 500 futures for his account and then attempted to conceal this conduct.
Feld has neither admitted nor denied the findings, CME said.
CME also said it had suspended Glenn Laken for five days and fined him $10,000.
CME's Business Conduct Committee, Financial Division, found that Laken had punched and severely injured another member in the S&P futures pit, the exchange said.
